'''Dimitrie D. Stancu''' (11 February 1927 – 17 April 2014) was a Romanian mathematician and professor. His work primarily focused on [[numerical analysis]] and approximation theories.<ref name="MacTutor">{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=J J |last2=Robertson |first2=E F |date=November 2014 |title=Dimitrie D Stancu |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Stancu/ |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=MacTutor}}</ref> During his career, he served as the Member of the Scientific Council of the Institute from 1990 until 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dimitrie D. Stancu (1927-2014) |url=https://ictp.acad.ro/dimitrie-d-stancu/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Tiberiu Popoviciu Institute of Numerical Analysis |language=en-US}}</ref> He then published his works at the [[Babeș-Bolyai University|Babes-Bolyai University]] in 1977.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=GENERAL MATHEMATICS |url=https://generalmathematics.ro/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Vol22_no1_2014_Roger.pdf |access-date=January 17, 2026}}</ref> 

== Early life and education ==
Dimitrie D. Stancu was born on 11 February 1927 in [[Orțișoara|Călacea]], Timiș County. His father had died prior, leaving his mother to take care of him. He began to work as a [[shepherd]]. His brother, a painter who worked in [[Arad, Romania|Arad]], took him to an orphanage in Arad in 1937 when he was 10 years old. He was then brought up by a family some time later.<ref name="MacTutor"/><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2013 |title=ACADEMICIAN PROFESSOR DIMITRIE D. STANCU AT HIS 85-TH ANNIVERSARY |url=https://www.cs.ubbcluj.ro/~studia-i/contents/2013-1/01-DDStancu.pdf |archive-date= |access-date=January 17, 2026}}</ref>

Stancu moved to [[Cluj]] where he studied at [[Victor Babeș University]] in 1947 under his supervisor [[Tiberiu Popoviciu]], and graduated in 1951.<ref name=":1" /> After his graduation, he was appointed to the Department of Mathematical Analysis of Babeș University. He obtained a [[PhD]] in 1956.<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
Between 1961 and 1962, he was tasked by the [[Romanian Ministry of Education]] to undertake research in the Department of Numerical Analysis at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]], conducted by [[Preston C Hammer]]. When he returned to Romania, he was named full professor of the Numerical and Statistical Calculus Chair from the Faculty of Mathematics at the Babeș-Bolyai University.<ref name="MacTutor"/> In 1968, he studied and introduced a new linear equation known as the "fundamental polynomials of Stancu”.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=D.D. STANCU OPERATORS |url=https://math.ubbcluj.ro/~mathjour/fulltext/2014-2/radu.pdf |access-date=January 17, 2026}}</ref>

During his career, he wrote over 120 papers of research dedicated to mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academician prof. univ. dr. Dimitrie D. Stancu {{!}} Facultatea de Matematică și Informatică |trans-title=Academician Prof. Dr. Dimitrie D. Stancu |url=https://www.cs.ubbcluj.ro/academician-prof-univ-dr-dimitrie-d-stancu/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |language=ro-RO}}</ref> In 1999, he was elected an honorary member of the [[Romanian Academy]], with the [[University of Sibiu]] and the [[North University of Baia Mare]] titling him as [[Doctor Honoris Causa]] alongside.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=In memoriam professor Dimitrie D. Stancu, honorary member of the Romanian Academy |url=https://ictp.acad.ro/jnaat/journal/article/view/2014-vol43-no2-art1/In%20memoriam%20DD%20Stancu |journal=Journal of Numerical Analysis and Approximation Theory |volume=43 |issue=2 |pages=2}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Stancu married mathematician Felicia. They later had two daughters, Angela Stancu (born 1957) and Mirela (born 1958), both of whom became teachers. Stancu died on 17 April 2014 in [[Cluj-Napoca|Cluj]]. He was 87.<ref name="MacTutor" />
